newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait to privatise $3.3bln worth of firms.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait to privatise $3.3bln worth of firms.

text.p: Kuwait plans to privatise another 18 local firms in the next two years worth one billion dinars ($3.3 billion), an official was quoted on Saturday as saying.
The head of the state Kuwait Investment Authority, Ali al- Badr, told the Arab Times that since 1994 the government had sold holdings in more than 20 firms for 750 million dinars.

Al-Watan newspaper on Saturday quoted Communications, Electricity and Water Minister Jassem al-Oun as saying that the government was eager to privatise telecommunications, urging parliament "to swiftly look into this issue because it has been long delayed without a reason."
Parliament has been presented by a draft law to approve the next and more complex stage of privatising heavily-subsidised public service firms which are used as employment centres for Kuwaitis.

He urged MPs to "liberate themselves from the fear of privatisation", assuring them that there was no reason for concern over the future of employment for Kuwaitis or fear of a sharp rise in the price of services.
